title: Content hash explainer
prompt: A 45-second narrated explainer that teaches what a content hash is and why it makes renders resumable. Clean, friendly, diagram-led. Captions on screen.
goal: leave the viewer able to say what a content hash is and why a render keyed on one can stop and resume without redoing work
audience: developers and technical readers on a documentation page or in a team channel

subject.description: a diagram card on a paper stage, one card per step

narration.script:
What is a content hash, and why does it let a render pick up where it stopped?
A long render is thousands of frames, and a crash used to mean starting over.
A content hash is a fingerprint of the inputs: the shot, the look, the code and the tools.
Every shot renders into a folder named by its hash, and each finished frame is checked in with its own hash.
When a render stops, the next run reads that ledger, skips what is on disk, and renders only what is missing.
A crash costs one frame, not a night, and a change re-renders only the shots it touched.
Hash the inputs, name the output by the hash, and the work you did stays done.

limitsAcknowledged: diagram-led is read as typographic diagrams: a labelled card on a 2.5D paper stage per step, with the numbers, the hash and the file names as type; no illustration engine draws arrows or icons
captions on screen are the narration's own sentences, burnt into the frame at the bottom from the SRT the voice produced
the narration is the local English voice af_heart; the user's own recording is the alternative
no music: none was supplied and nothing is downloaded
